q: Coding agents increasingly undertake development tasks in mature enterprise repositories, yet existing benchmarks offer limited insight into whether they fulfill complete Product Requirement Documents (PRDs)
r: Include: PACE-Bench evaluates agents building to full PRDs at feature level and contributes an evaluation methodology.
EC6: tasks are SWE-Bench style issue repair, driven by a user simulator; issue repair is always excluded.

q: We used Claude Code to migrate ten PyTorch research projects from GPUs to TPUs and verified each migration level by level with the L0–L4 consistency hierarchy.
r: Include: Claude Code agent changes project code, and the L0-L4 consistency hierarchy is a new evaluation method (EC6 ii).

q: We qualitatively annotated 325 experiments reported in 146 peer-reviewed full papers published between 2025 and 2026.
r: Include: secondary study of how agentic coding evaluations control harness, model and cost, directly relevant to RQ3.

q: Second, we introduce Foresight-SWE, a benchmark built from real PR pairs where an initial change introduces a defect that is repaired only by a later PR.
r: EC6: SWE-bench style benchmark mined from PR pairs and fixes, i.e. defect repair, not feature or project building.

q: SWEBench (Jimenez et al., 2024) for code repair, SWT-Bench (Mündler et al., 2024) for test case generation
r: EC6: harness self-evolution studied on issue repair and test generation datasets; not application development.

q: We construct realistic compiler construction workflows with strict serial dependencies
r: Include: long-horizon compiler construction with cost, quality and robustness metrics for comparing agents; project-level and evaluation-method contribution.

q: For code review, we use the patch-level review dataset released with Hydra-Reviewer
r: EC6: code generation on LiveCodeBench problems and code review; small tasks and code review, not application development.

q: The tasks that we study lie between code completion and repository-level tasks.
r: EC6: competitive-programming LiveCodeBench problems, function-level tasks, not application development.

q: We introduced MT-Web2Code, the first multi-turn multimodal benchmark for iterative web UI coding
r: Include: new benchmark with evaluation protocol for coding agents editing web page code (EC6 ii).
